name: Kirsch Edge Response
algorithm: Kirsch Edge Response — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method applies Kirsch edge operators for image forensic analysis:

1. **Kirsch Compass Kernel Application**: Eight directional Kirsch kernels (3×3) are convolved with the image, each detecting edges in one of eight compass directions (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). The maximum response across all eight directions gives the edge magnitude at each pixel.

2. **Edge Direction Analysis**: The direction of maximum Kirsch response indicates the local edge orientation. In authentic images, edge orientations follow scene geometry and object boundaries. AI-generated images may show edge direction anomalies — directions that don't correspond to coherent object boundaries.

3. **Edge Magnitude Distribution**: The statistical distribution of Kirsch edge magnitudes is analyzed. Natural camera images show characteristic edge magnitude distributions shaped by the lens MTF and sensor resolution. AI-generated images may show different distributions — either too many weak edges (from generation smoothing) or edge magnitude patterns inconsistent with optical imaging.

4. **Edge Continuity Assessment**: Real object edges produce continuous Kirsch responses along their length. The method checks edge continuity — AI generation may produce fragmented edges or edges that appear and disappear without physical justification, especially at boundaries of generated regions.

5. **Multi-Directional Edge Coherence**: The coherence of edge responses across the eight Kirsch directions is analyzed. At true edges, one or two adjacent directions dominate. AI artifacts may produce diffuse edge responses across multiple directions, indicating non-physical edge structures detectable through directional coherence analysis.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through kirsch edge response analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used
